---
title: "The native pipe does not know the magrittr dot"
ref: PIP-01
categories: [Pipes]
impact: cryptique
extrait: 'quote(words |> gsub("a", "b", .))'
attendu: "`gsub(\"a\", \"b\", words)`, as with `%>%`"
versions: "Since R 4.1.0 (native pipe); the `_` placeholder exists since R 4.2.0"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2023)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
words <- c("abc", "bab")
words |> gsub("a", "b", .)
quote(words |> gsub("a", "b", .))
```
:::

## Why

With the {magrittr} `%>%`, the dot stands for the value coming down the pipe, and its presence prevents insertion in first position. The native pipe `|>` has no such rule: it always inserts the value as the first argument, and the dot remains a plain variable name.

`quote()` shows the call actually built: `words` becomes the pattern, `"a"` the replacement, `"b"` the text, and `.` is passed as the fourth argument. If no `.` variable exists, the error "object '.' not found" says nothing about the pipe. If a `.` variable is lying around in the environment, the computation runs and gives a wrong result.

## The remedy

Since R 4.2.0, the native pipe has its own placeholder, `_`, which must be passed to a named argument.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
words |> gsub(pattern = "a", replacement = "b", x = _)
```
:::
